label: models/fw_valvewheel.mdl: a valve wheel, red paint worn to steel at the rim

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_longjump.mdl, models/rip.mdl, models/uplant1.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, B, C, D where the asset was C, A, B, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Front and back views show a round wheel of about 32 units with four straight spokes to a central hub. The left, right and top views show the rim edge-on as a flat bar, with the axle stub through the hub. This matches a valve wheel's outline as the brief describes it. No part sticks out or is missing in any of the ten views.

M2.reason: Measured size is 14.2 x 32.4 x 32.4 against the brief's 32 across, which is 1.1% off, well inside 15%. The 14.2 depth is not a size the brief gives.

M3.reason: Parts the brief names, checked down to the small ones: a full rim ring, four spokes (counted in the front and back views), a central hub with a hexagonal steel cap, and an axle stub on both sides of the hub (left and right views). Small rim joints show as grey tabs at 3 and 9 o'clock in the front and back views. All are present in the right places. The brief names no rivets, claws or teeth, and the rim's facet count is not given.

M4.reason: Red painted metal on the rim, spokes and hub, with grey steel showing as worn bands along the rim faces and a grey hex cap on the hub. This is the brief's red paint worn to steel at the rim, and the colours agree across the views.

M5.reason: The worn steel bands sit on the rim's faces in the front, back and oblique views. Dark cracks and wear marks sit on the rim in the front and back views. The hub cap is crisp. The wear reads at a similar sharpness, with nothing extra added.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric. The four-way line-up put to other judges picked the asset (B) once in four readings, the other three picks going to the wrong pictures. Not measured as a catch, so it is not held lower.

M7.reason: The wheel stands upright, face on in the front view, with its rim vertical in the left and right views. Its axle runs through the hub at the origin. The brief gives no facing for the wheel, so this is read as a valve wheel stands.

M8.reason: SMAK check is clean (no errors), and no open, inside-out or floating part shows in any of the ten views. Triangles are 376, under the 422 Valve's most-triangled prop of this kind and size uses, so the amended M8 passes. The count is past the third quartile (156), which is the kit's warning, not a fail.
